sections.html: Common name: Olmecan Blue-Eye. Bred fish are available at 4–5 cm. The fish are very peaceful and should always be kept in groups.

The genus Priapella currently comprises 6 described species, of which P. intermedia and P. compressa are found occasionally in the ornamental fish trade. Keeping these fish in a home aquarium is not difficult at all.
The water temperature should be between 21 and 26°C. Medium hard to hard water and a pH over 7.5 is preferred.
The tank should be well lit and filtered.
Priapella olmecae feeds readily on any usual food for ornamental fish, but never from the bottom.

All Priapella species are surface dwellers that live in the wild in comparatively strong current. Here they swim in swarms, head against the current and jump for small insects that form the biggest part of their natural diet. The blue eyes of all species are very conspicuous. They shine so brightly that one is reminded of the lampeyes of the genus Aplocheilichthys.

The fish are very peaceful and should always be kept in groups. Plants are not harmed by this species.

Lexicon: Priapella means "tiny penis", referring to the male's gonopodium. intermedia means "in between". compressa means "compressed". olmecae refers to the indigenous people in Mexico, the Olmecs. Aplocheilichthys means "fish that is similar to Aplocheilus"; Aplocheilus is another genus of fish.
